name: DT Overlay Builder
blurb: a device tree overlay fragment to enable, add or change nodes on a base tree
intro: Builds a device tree overlay against a pasted base tree: pick the target node, set its status and properties, add I2C, SPI, LED or UART child nodes from templates, and get the /plugin/ source in both the &label and fragment@N/__overlay__ forms with the line that loads it. It checks the target exists, bus cells, I2C reserved and duplicate addresses, chip selects already taken (spidev), missing compatibles and undefined phandle labels.

inputs.label: Base tree (DTS)
inputs.help: The board's tree, merged: dtc -I dtb -O dts of its .dtb, or /proc/device-tree via dtc -I fs.

inputs.label: Target
inputs.help: A label (&i2c1) or a path (&{/soc/i2c@7e804000}); &{/} for the root.

inputs.label: Properties to set
inputs.help: Values in DTS (<1 2>, "text", &label) or a bare number (becomes <n>) or text (becomes "text").

inputs.label: Child nodes to add
inputs.help: i2c: addr = 7-bit address; spi: addr = chip select, param = spi-max-frequency; gpio-led: addr = line ("17 low" for active-low), param = trigger, ref = GPIO controller; pwm-led: addr = channel, param = period ns, ref = PWM controller; uart: param = current-speed; extra: "k = v; flag".

inputs.label: Also disable
inputs.help: Labels to set to disabled in extra fragments (e.g. the spidev on the CS you take).

inputs.label: Root compatible (fragment form)
inputs.help: Raspberry Pi overlays carry the SoC compatible; leave empty for others.

examples.title: BME280 on the Raspberry Pi 4's I2C1 at 400 kHz

input.name: bme280-i2c1

examples.title: MCP3008 ADC on SPI0 CS0, taking over from spidev0

input.name: mcp3008-spi0

usage: Give base (the board's merged DTS), target (&label or /path), status (keep/okay/disabled), props [{name, value}], children [{kind: i2c|spi|gpio-led|pwm-led|uart|custom, name, compatible, addr, param, ref, extra}], optional alsoDisable/alsoEnable label lists, the overlay name and loader (rpi/uboot/extlinux/yocto). It returns the overlay source in texts 'Overlay (&label form)' and 'Overlay (fragment form)' with macros expanded to numbers (dtc has no preprocessor), 'Load it' with the commands, a fragment table, and warnings for an unknown target, wrong bus cells, reserved or taken I2C addresses and chip selects, missing compatibles and labels the base does not define. Use it to write an overlay for a board you have the DTS of.
sources: NXP UM10204 I2C-bus specification rev. 7, table 4 (reserved addresses); include/dt-bindings/i2c/i2c.h I2C_TEN_BIT_ADDRESS
bindings/leds/leds-gpio.yaml, leds-pwm.yaml; include/dt-bindings/gpio/gpio.h, interrupt-controller/irq.h, pwm/pwm.h (macro values)
Raspberry Pi documentation, 'Device Trees, overlays and parameters' (config.txt dtoverlay=, dtoverlay command)
U-Boot doc/usage/fdt_overlays.rst (fdt apply) and doc/develop/distro.rst (extlinux fdtoverlays)
